questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To me, it was important to choose a well-recommended university. I knew that other public health students had great experiences at SFU. I was told that SFU offered both great academic opportunities and was very helpful during the whole process. Also, live somewhere with beautiful nature and opportunities to travel.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would rate my stay at SFU 10/10. However, the overall rate was 8/10. The reason why is that it was stressful and difficult to plan during the COVID-pandemic (I was going just then the Omnicron-variant spread across the world). I was from time to time unsure of whenever I would be able to go. It takes a lot of time to plan everything – and I found it sometimes difficult to get the needed help from KU. But I would never choose to stay home just because there is a lot of planning. It is worth it all and you will forget all of it once you arrive!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Simon Fraser University was very helpfull and sends out a lot of emails with all the information needed. Whenever in doubt, I send an email and got an answere the same day.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The introduction to exchange students was online due to COVID. Also, I received a lot of emails with information about travel, housing, immigration, arrival, registration of courses, social gatherings for exchange students, online “get-ready”-seminars etc. 
Also, I callled them if I had a quick question before going. Once I arrived, I just went to the front desk.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: My overall experience was that they were very helpful! My home university was also helpful – but it was at times VERY difficult to get in contact with KU.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms and small apartments (in Townhouse).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Both. I chose to buy the mealplan because all of my friends lived in facilities where the mealplan was mandatory.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live on campus. SFU is building a lot of new housing facilities these years.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in Shell House. It was old and a bit worn out. It had a great kitchen if you wanted to cook. You need to bring/or buy your own pans, dishes, cutlery, etc. I would recommend living on campus. The Townhouses are quite popular to live in and I would apply for those if I was going again.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot to do in the registration process - but they were good at explaining what should be done when and how.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will receive an email with information about applying for SFU. Here you will be asked to list 8 courses that you would like to take. I would recommend applying for housing when you do this. Later, my application was accepted, and I received my ‘Letter of Admission'. SFU rewelded which of the 8 courses I was able to attend. I would then apply for those courses and SFU would enroll all exchange students based on this. I had to change some courses before going because I could not get all of them approved by KU. SFU was very helpful doing so. I just send an email and the problem solved within a day.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Webpage, emails from the international exchange department at SFU, online seminars, etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 3 of 8 courses that I applied for at SFU was not created. I decided to apply for prior credit for 4 of the remaining courses from KU. KU approved only three of these, which is why I had to choose a new one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for courses that you find interesting at SFU. You can always change courses once you get there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was somewhat the same or easier - depending on the specific course. But the workload was much higher. You have to do a lot more through out the semester. On the other hand, the final exame does not count as much as in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot more focus on participation. I had to do mandatory weekly quizzes - don't worry they were very easy. Also, I had to write papers in all courses before midterm and final exams. They focus a lot on this too.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HSCI 120 - Introduction to Human Sexuality and Sexual Behavior
HSCI 206 - Health Economics
HSCI 305 - The Canadian Health Care System
HSCI 408 - Plagues, Poverty, and Pollutants - The Origins and Evolution of Public Health.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would defently recommend HSCI 120, HSCI 206 and HSCI 408. All the professors are great and the courses are interesting. Also, the workload, papers, midterms and final exams are manageable. HSCI 305 is interesting from a public health perspective but it is only and the workload is really heavy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive to live in Canada than I expected. I don't recall any unexpected costs from SFU. But I was supprised of how expensive it was to travel, shop, etc. Remember to apply for scholarships!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was less expensive to live on campus than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My stay was to some extent still affected by COVID - not all students clubs had activities due to COVID. SFU is a great place to go if you like sports and nature. There are lot to do.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Fitness center, swimming pool, track, etc. They host a lot of social gatherings among students in the Convocation Mall. Also, there are plenty of studentclubs to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of the U-Pass (transportation card that you buy through SFU) and go around Vancouver. Go to Whistler and ski. If you like skiing and plan on doing it a lot: Buy a season pass to Whistler before going. They are sold out quickly in the late fall/early winter. Do not wait until upon arrival. Get some local friends and get their recommendations for traveling.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go watch NHL and explore nature. I went on a whale-watching tour in mid-April and saw orcas. It was so cool! Go to Lynn Canyon and hike. Eat at Granville. Take the ferry to Bowen Island and hike. Go to Vancouver Island.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Canadians are really welcoming and helpful

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live on campus and make friends with those you live with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The local students are usually younger than exchange students. It was not a challenge but just a difference that I experienced.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their welcoming, warm and helpful attitude.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) apply for housing on campus, 2) if possible: choose courses that give you Friday off (nice if you want to go on trips on the weekends), 3) apply for scholarships, 4) ENJOY!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid of just sending an email or calling them when in doubt.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Got to know a lot of kind and sweet people, while traveling in Canada and had an overall successful stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The planning before going - but don't be scared: It is all worth it!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you consider going on exchange - do it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
